correctness.rationale: Stationary single-site distributions have a negative-binomial time-slice PGF mixed by independent exponential reset ages. Taking v->infinity gives the exact level PGF. At the sublinear-reset critical edge, the rescaled PGF tends by dominated convergence to exp[-exp(1/u)E1(1/u)]; nonnegative factorial cumulants give uniform high scaled moments and dominated convergence under uniform level sampling. The n^(-1/nu) Pareto tail and moment threshold follow by layer-cake. 17 reproducible auxiliary checks passed; the proof is analytic.

value.rationale: Natural stationary total population at a uniformly sampled fitness level has a complete heavy-tail law even without mean condensation; an explicitly characterized universal edge scaling law gives all moment thresholds and sharp coefficients 3/C^2 and 19/C^3. That distinguishes rare large level loads from known within-microstate pair crowding and is meaningful for model selection, network degrees, and finite-mean but high-risk population load.
